question: The compound interest earned in 1 year on ₹2,40,000 at the rate of 40% per annum, compounded quarterly, is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Quarterly Rate = 40% ÷ 4 = **10%** | Time = 4 quarters.

Successive percentage for 10% for 4 periods = **46.41%**.

Compound Interest = 2,40,000 × 46.41/100

CI = 2,400 × 46.41 = **₹1,11,384**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,11,384.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Principal (P) = **₹2,40,000**, Rate (R) = **40% p.a.**, Time (T) = **1 year**.

**Formula:** Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ | CI = A − P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eca99b6ef0123a20e1ddf2594b062cbeb8f57fae37eca8730bacc6b0b3c21bc2.png] 

⇒ Quarterly Rate (r) = 40% ÷ 4 = 10%

⇒ Number of quarters (n) = 1 × 4 = 4

⇒ Amount (A) = 2,40,000 × (1 + 10/100)⁴

⇒ A = 2,40,000 × (1.1)⁴

⇒ A = 2,40,000 × 1.4641 = 3,51,384

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

⇒ CI = 3,51,384 − 2,40,000 = 1,11,384

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,11,384.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of Interest

When interest is compounded **quarterly**, the effective annual rate is (1 + r/400)⁴ − 1.

Compounding Frequency

As the frequency of compounding increases (daily > monthly > quarterly > yearly), the **Compound Interest** earned also increases for the same rate and principal.

Rule of 72

To find the approximate time needed to double your money, divide 72 by the annual **interest rate** (72 ÷ R).
